root_cause.text: In RDMA/irdma, irdma_create_user_ah() placed a stack-allocated struct irdma_create_ah_resp on the user response path without initializing its reserved rsvd[4] field, causing uninitialized stack bytes to be copied to userspace via ib_respond_udata().
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp;` to `struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp = {};`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that only `ah_id` was set while `rsvd[4]` was “NEVER SET” and “The reserved members of the structure were not zeroed.”

agent_logs.root_cause_candidate: In RDMA/irdma, irdma_create_user_ah() placed a stack-allocated struct irdma_create_ah_resp on the user response path without initializing its reserved rsvd[4] field, causing uninitialized stack bytes to be copied to userspace via ib_respond_udata().
agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch changes `struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp;` to `struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp = {};`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that only `ah_id` was set while `rsvd[4]` was “NEVER SET” and “The reserved members of the structure were not zeroed.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Zero-initialize the AH response structure to avoid leaking or using uninitialized stack contents in user response data.
intent_record.what: The local variable declaration `struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp;` was changed to `struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp = {};`, adding zero-initialization of the entire response structure at declaration time.
intent_record.how: This ensures all fields in `uresp`, including any reserved or conditionally assigned members, start as zero before use, preventing uninitialized stack data from being returned or consumed and making the generated response deterministic.

grouping_result.intent: Zero-initialize the AH response structure to avoid leaking or using uninitialized stack contents in user response data.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by zero-initializing the AH response structure before it is copied to userspace, preventing leakage of uninitialized stack data in the reserved field.

candidates.rationale: This stack-allocated response structure is declared without initialization, leaving fields such as rsvd[4] uninitialized. Because this structure is later returned to userspace, the uninitialized bytes can be leaked via the response path.

vuln_statements.explanation: This declares the user response structure on the stack without initialization. Because irdma_create_user_ah() later returns this structure to userspace, the uninitialized reserved field rsvd[4] can contain stale stack bytes and be leaked through ib_respond_udata().

Author: Mustafa Ismail <mustafa.ismail@intel.com>
Date:   Mon Feb 28 12:36:50 2022 -0600

    RDMA/irdma: Add support for address handle re-use
    
    Address handles (AH) are a limited HW resource and some user applications
    may create large numbers of identical AH's.  Avoid running out of AH's by
    reusing existing identical ones.
    
    Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20220228183650.290-1-shiraz.saleem@intel.com

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the full newly introduced `irdma_create_user_ah()` function and the exact user response handling. The vulnerable construct is present there: `struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp;` declares a stack variable without initialization, and later only `uresp.ah_id = ah->sc_ah.ah_info.ah_idx;` is assigned before `ib_copy_to_udata(udata, &uresp, min(sizeof(uresp), udata->outlen));`. Per the root cause, the response struct contains a reserved `rsvd[4]` field; since the struct is not zero-initialized, those reserved bytes can contain uninitialized stack data and be copied to userspace. There is no fix present such as `struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp = {};`, `memset(&uresp, 0, sizeof(uresp));`, or copying only the initialized field. Therefore this commit version contains the bug and does not yet contain the fix.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant function is present and fully visible: `static int irdma_create_ah(...)`. Inside it, the user response object is declared as `struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp;` with no initializer, so it is stack-allocated and not zeroed. Later, on the user response path, only one field is assigned: `uresp.ah_id = ah->sc_ah.ah_info.ah_idx;` and then the whole struct is copied out with `ib_copy_to_udata(udata, &uresp, min(sizeof(uresp), udata->outlen));`. Given the root cause that `struct irdma_create_ah_resp` contains reserved field `rsvd[4]`, those reserved bytes remain uninitialized and can be exposed to userspace. There is no fix present such as `struct irdma_create_ah_resp uresp = {};` or `memset(&uresp, 0, sizeof(uresp));` before copying to userspace.
